newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL one-mth interbank rate up after intervention.
newsitem.headline: KL one-mth interbank rate up after intervention.

text.p: The one-month interbank rate rose to 7.08/15 percent against 7.00/05 after Bank Negara intervened in the market to borrow for a one-month deposit, dealers said on Friday.
They said other interbank rates were mostly unchanged.
Dealers said one-month interbank rate was threatening to go below 7.05 percent after opening at 7.10/15, when the central bank decided to intervene much later than its usual time.
Bank Negara intervened at an unchanged 7.05 percent mainly to mop up excess liquidity in the system, dealers said.
Bank Negara regularly intervenes in the domestic money market to either keep liquidity under check or set interest rates.
The falling rates, despite a large outgo of funds from the system on Monday, had attracted central bank intervention.
Banks paid out two billion ringgit for a seven-year government bond issue and also completed their fortnightly topping up of statutory reserve accounts with the central bank on Monday.
But dealers said financial institutions had covered excessively for the bond issue and overseas funds were making a comeback to the market, which was keeping rates under pressure.
"The main reason (for the liquidity) was the recent inflows of funds into the forward market following the gains in the Malaysian ringgit," said research firm I.D.E.A. in a research note.
It said the decline in swap points after the ringgit's gains also suggested that interest rates were heading lower.
"The one-week money has fallen by more than one percent to 6.40 this morning (this week)," I.D.E.A said.
One-week money was at 6.60/70 percent after the tender, while two-week at 6.70/80, three-month at 7.20/25 and six-month at 7.25/30, were all unchanged from before.
Dealers said the overnight rate, which has been steady at 6.0 percent this week, may rise marginally only if the volume of the central bank intervention was large.
